'''Manijeh Razeghi''' is an Iranian-American scientist in the fields of [[semiconductor]]s and [[optoelectronic devices]]. She influenced modern epitaxial techniques for semiconductors such as low pressure [[MOCVD|metalorganic chemical vapor deposition (MOCVD)]], vapor phase epitaxy (VPE), [[Molecular-beam epitaxy|molecular beam epitaxy (MBE)]], GasMBE, and [[MOMBE]]. These techniques have enabled the development of semiconductor devices and quantum structures with higher composition consistency and reliability, leading to major advancement in InP and GaAs based quantum [[photonics]] and electronic devices, which were at the core of the late 20th century [[optical fiber]] telecommunications and early information technology.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Center for Quantum Devices - Director, Professor Manijeh Razeghi|url=http://cqd.ece.northwestern.edu/people/razeghi.php|website=cqd.ece.northwestern.edu|access-date=2020-05-20}}</ref>

Her current research interests include III-Nitride semiconductor devices, [[quantum cascade laser]]s, [[Quantum well infrared photodetector|quantum well infrared photodetectors (QWIP)]], and self assembled [[quantum dot]] devices.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Razeghi, Manijeh {{!}} Faculty {{!}} Northwestern Engineering|url=https://www.mccormick.northwestern.edu/research-faculty/directory/profiles/razeghi-manijeh.html|website=www.mccormick.northwestern.edu|access-date=2020-05-20}}</ref>

==Career==
Razeghi received a bachelor's degree in nuclear physics from [[University of Tehran|Tehran University]], then her doctorate from [[University of Paris|Université de Paris]], France. In 1986, she became the head of [[Thomson-CSF]] Exploratory Materials Lab and made a major contribution to the field of semiconductor physics when she developed [[Metalorganic vapour-phase epitaxy|metalorganic chemical vapor deposition (MOCVD)]] epitaxial technique and published her pioneering work on InP in her book "The MOCVD Challenge Volume 1: A Survey of GaInAsP-InP for Photonic and Electronic Applications" (Adam Hilger Press, 1989).<ref>{{Cite book|last=Razeghi|first=Manijeh|title=The MOCVD Challenge: Volume 1|date=2010-08-17|publisher=CRC Press|isbn=978-0-429-07555-1|doi=10.1201/9781439807002}}</ref>

In 1991, Razeghi moved to the US to become the Walter P. Murphy Professor and director of the Center for Quantum Devices, Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science, Northwestern University,<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.mccormick.northwestern.edu/research-faculty/directory/profiles/razeghi-manijeh.html|title=Razeghi, Manijeh - Faculty - Northwestern Engineering|website=www.mccormick.northwestern.edu|access-date=2018-04-24}}</ref> where she continued her research in quantum devices such as lasers and photodetectors. In 1995, she published her second book "The MOCVD Challenge Volume 2: A Survey of GaInAsP-GaAs for Photonic and Electronic Device Applications" (Institute of Physics Publishing, 1995).<ref>{{Cite book|last=Razeghi|first=Manijeh|title=The MOCVD Challenge: Volume 2|date=1995-01-01|publisher=CRC Press|isbn=978-0-429-07685-5|doi=10.1201/9781482289381}}</ref>

In 2018, Professor Razeghi won the [[Benjamin Franklin Medal (Franklin Institute)|Benjamin Franklin Medal]] for Electrical Engineering for "the realization of high-power terahertz frequency sources operating at room temperature<ref>{{Cite web|last=UNIVERSITY|first=MANIJEH RAZEGHI, WENJIA ZHOU, DONGHAI WU, RYAN MCCLINTOCK AND STEVEN SLIVKEN, NORTHWESTERN|title=Quantum Cascade Laser Breakthrough for Advanced Remote Detection|url=https://www.photonics.com/Articles/Quantum_Cascade_Laser_Breakthrough_for_Advanced/a61166|access-date=2020-09-01|website=www.photonics.com}}</ref> using specially designed and manufactured semiconductor lasers, which enables a new generation of imagers, chemical/biological sensors, and ultra-broadband wireless communication systems."<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fi.edu/laureates/manijeh-razeghi|title=The Franklin Institute Awards|date=March 15, 2018}}</ref> She developed lasers that can detect explosives and pathogens<ref>{{Cite web|title=StackPath|url=https://www.laserfocusworld.com/test-measurement/research/article/16565025/new-quantum-cascade-laser-resonator-has-highpower-singlemode-emission|access-date=2020-09-01|website=www.laserfocusworld.com|date=24 August 2012 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=New terahertz source could strengthen sensing applications|url=https://phys.org/news/2016-03-terahertz-source-applications.html|access-date=2020-09-01|website=phys.org|language=en}}</ref> as well as electronic devices that will eventually deliver turbo-charged, super-fast WiFi.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Wang |first=Hui |last2=Yu |first2=Cun |date=2024-07-15 |title=Light People: Professor Manijeh Razeghi |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/s41377-023-01343-8 |journal=Light: Science & Applications |language=en |publisher=Nature Publishing Group |volume=13 |issue=1 |pages=164 |doi=10.1038/s41377-023-01343-8  |doi-access=free|issn=2047-7538}}</ref>

She holds 60 patents <ref>{{Cite web|title=Manijeh Razeghi Inventions, Patents and Patent Applications - Justia Patents Search|url=https://patents.justia.com/inventor/manijeh-razeghi|website=patents.justia.com|language=en|access-date=2018-04-24}}</ref> and has published 20 books<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://cqd.eecs.northwestern.edu/pubs/books.php|title = Center for Quantum Devices - Books}}</ref> and more than 1000 papers.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Manijeh Razeghi - Google Scholar Citations|url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=9FAOXBIAAAAJ&hl=en|website=scholar.google.com|access-date=2018-04-24}}</ref>
